_doc: After the player dies (player/afterlife.js): who they can come back as, and how the world turns while they wait. stations: what each walk of life starts with as a new character (gold range, stat and skill bonuses on top of the base 5s and 1s). candidates: how many people are offered (at random, or of a chosen settlement); newcomer: a chosen settlement also offers someone just arriving from another town, with a mother tongue of their own.
_heirArrival: Where an heir takes up the mantle (player/heirArrival.js, from Relationships.succeedAsHeir): away on their years abroad, else a cadet head at the branch's seat, else the House's home nearest the death (a house it keeps, a settlement it holds), else in the town the ruler died in, else the nearest friendly town (not quarantined, no bounty there) — one with food on its stalls within foodSlack hexes further if there is one. They set out with provisionMeals of food: from the House's larder at home (larderFirst), then bought at the town's stalls with the heir's own purse. An abdication hands over in place.
_distant: The distant years: a wait of at least minDays (Let Time Pass) turns the world in coarser steps — every market, its trade, labour and diggings together once every marketSpan days, worked as that many days; each town's peoples' effects afresh every peoplesEvery days; the realms' slow reads (production profiles, stability targets, recruiting ground, the arms buyers, road floods) every realmEvery days. Same seed, same years; not the same as day by day.
